newsitem.title: GABON: Congo Brazzaville rivals meet face-to-face.
newsitem.headline: Congo Brazzaville rivals meet face-to-face.

text.p: Envoys of the Congo Republic's warring parties met face-to-face in Gabon on Friday to outline their thoughts on proposals for a peace deal, mediators said.
Representatives of President Pascal Lissouba gave their thoughts on the different options put forward by the mediators, U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun told reporters.
Envoys from his rival and predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso would do so on Saturday, he added.

In their troubled oil-producing nation's capital Brazzaville, a truce held and the radio station run by former military leader Sassou said that military commanders from the two sides had discussed joint patrols in the battle zone.
Sources close to the military talks at the French embassy in Brazzaville said the two sides would meet again on Saturday.
A showdown began on June 5 after the army surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias. Political and ethnic clashes killed hundreds of people.
Representatives of national mediator Bernard Kolelas, whose militia were in the thick of similar clashes after a disputed 1993 presidential election, have attended the various talks.
Lissouba and Sassou remain in Brazzaville.
Sassou's radio there said on Wednesday a sticking point was a decision by Congo's Constitutional Council to extend Lissouba's mandate until elections. His mandate ends at the end of August.
The council cancelled a planned July 27 presidential election. Sassou did not object to that but wants a government of national salvation.
